C0.quote: a novel hybrid of Representative Democracy and Direct Democracy
C0.note: Voting systems (elections of representatives plus weighted issue voting with delegation).

C1.quote: We provide NP-Hardness results for electing an ideal set of representatives
C1.note: AL: NP-hardness results. WD: rules evaluated against the majority-agreement objective. SI: simulations, which make up most results. OT: proposal of the FRD model, a main contribution of the paper.

C2.1.value: preferences / electoral preferences P_VC (approvals, complete rankings, weights); representatives' votes P_D; delegations P_VD
C2.1.quote: The voters express preferences over the candidates, collectively denoted by

C2.2.quote: electoral preferences PV C as either approvals or complete rankings
C2.2.note: CARD: normalized weights for the Max Agreement rule. OTH: binary issue votes of representatives, and fractional delegation weights.

C2.3.quote: each voter v j has a preference v ij ∈ {0, 1}
C2.3.note: Voters' issue preferences are held attitudes; in RD they are not submitted.

C2.4.quote: voters’ preferences over candidates are derived exactly from their agreement
C2.4.note: Issue preferences (v_j, P_V) and electoral inputs (P_VC) are separate objects with separate notation. The paper notes that the derivation assumption should be relaxed, so the two may differ.

C3.1.quote: Our analysis also did not examine strategic behavior by the voters

C3.2.quote: we assume that v approves of c if and only if
C3.2.note: Reported approvals and rankings are stated in words to follow exactly from voters' issue agreement.

C3.3.quote: We give the election rules the best chances we can
C3.3.note: The reason given is that this is a best-case assumption for the election rules.

C4.1.quote: each voter v j is assigned a preference intensity parameter
C4.1.note: Intensity for voters is used, so C4.1 applies. Intensity defines the Bernoulli parameter of issue preferences and the delegation probability. Rankings and approvals are defined from agreement L(v,c).

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: the majority of representatives agrees with the voter majority
C5.1.note: Majority agreement and coverage are representation-type criteria for voters.

C5.2.quote: We hold Direct Democracy with majority voting and full participation
C5.2.note: Majority agreement is evaluated against voters' issue preferences, which are separate from the submitted electoral inputs.

VOT.quote_behav: we assume that v prefers c to ĉ if they agree
VOT.note: Voters elect representatives and delegate according to fixed rules (incisive, Best Rep, Approve) or with fixed probabilities.

OTH.note: Elected representatives act as proxies receiving delegations; the codebook places delegates and proxies under VOT.

C7.1.note: Only one type (VOT, including representatives as proxies) is present.

claims.quote: reveal the potential for Flexible Representative Democracy to improve outcomes
the choice of election rule appears less important than the quality
taking the best of both worlds from Direct Democracy

C9.2.quote: Our analysis makes use of a toy model of agent preferences
C9.2.note: Stated: incisive delegation, impartial culture, and electoral preferences derived from issue agreement. Not stated in words: that representatives cast votes equal to their preferences; it is only implicit in the notation, with strategic behaviour acknowledged as not examined.

C1.reason: The paper's introduction of FRD as a new voting-system model is a main contribution, so OT applies alongside AL, WD and SI.

C2.4.reason: Held issue preferences and submitted electoral inputs have separate notation, and the link between them is an explicit assumption the paper says could be relaxed.

C3.2.reason: The paper explicitly states that reported approvals and rankings follow exactly from held issue preferences.

C3.3.reason: The stated justification is a best-case assumption for the rules, which fits none of the listed reason categories.

C4.1.reason: Voter preference intensity is used, so the item applies, and its relation to the inputs is formally defined.

C5.2.reason: Outcomes are evaluated against voters' issue preferences, which are defined separately from the electoral inputs submitted to the rule.

C6.OTH.reason: Representatives in FRD function as proxies, which the codebook assigns to VOT rather than OTH.

C7.1.reason: With representatives coded under VOT, fewer than two types are present.
